questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
The transition of the former Soviet Union from a planned economy towards a market economy was accompanied by a reduction in the proportion of incomes that households saved. What could explain this?

options.A: an increase in income inequality
options.B: an increase in job insecurity
options.C: increased availability of consumer goods
options.D: the introduction of charges for hospital treatment

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the production possibility curve of a desert island economy where the inhabitants live off just two commodities, coconuts and fish. coconuts O fish What explains the shape of the production possibility curve?

options.A: Coconuts and fish are in joint demand.
options.B: Coconuts and fish are perfect substitutes when consumed.
options.C: Fishing and coconut growing are equally efficient.
options.D: The opportunity cost of fish falls as more time is devoted to fishing.

questions.questionText: Three women work in a pottery workshop, each dividing their time equally between three products. The table shows how many units of each product are made. plates bowls mugs Jane 100 50 50 Sarah 50 100 50 Seema 50 50 100 total 200 200 200 Later, division of labour is introduced and each woman makes only the product in which she has absolute advantage. What is the rise in total output?

options.A: 150 units B 300 units C 600 units D 900 units

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a demand curve for a good. price D O quantity Which statement describes the nature of this demand curve?

options.A: A greater or smaller quantity is demanded as price changes.
options.B: A lower price is the result of a fall in demand.
options.C: As demand increases so does price.
options.D: Quantity changes in proportion to the change in price.

questions.questionText: Assume that Tiger Woods, a famous golfer, announces that his final golf appearance will be at the next US Open Tournament. How might this affect the demand for tickets for the tournament?

options.A: It will cause a movement downward along the demand curve.
options.B: It will cause a movement upward along the demand curve.
options.C: It will cause a shift to the left in the position of the demand curve.
options.D: It will cause a shift to the right in the position of the demand curve.

questions.questionText: A survey into the market for good X found that it is an inferior good and a close substitute to good Y. Which values for the income elasticity of demand for good X and its cross elasticity of demand with respect to the price of good Y would support this? cross elasticity of demand income elasticity of for good X with respect to demand for good X the price of good Y
The diagram shows the demand curve for a product with unitary price elasticity. price D O quantity What will happen with such a curve?

options.A: A fall in price will bring about an increase in total expenditure on the product.
options.B: A fall in price will bring about an increase in sales but a fall in total expenditure on the product.
options.C: As the price rises, total expenditure on the product stays the same.
options.D: As the price rises, total expenditure on the product rises and then falls.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the effect on the market for rice of a change in government policy that causes a shift in the supply curve from S to S . S S L price K J M D O quantity What does the area JKLM represent?

options.A: the cost to the government of a subsidy to rice growers
options.B: the extra saving to importers of the removal of a tariff on rice
options.C: the increase in consumer surplus from the introduction of a maximum price for rice
options.D: the loss in government revenue from the reduction in a lump sum tax on rice

questions.questionText: The price of a firm’s product rises by 12%. After one week the firm is only able to produce the same quantity but after one month it can increase the quantity by 6%. How would the price elasticity of supply be described after one week and after one month? after one week after one month

options.A: infinite elastic
options.B: infinite inelastic
options.C: zero elastic
options.D: zero inelastic

questions.questionText: Many people used to smoke in restaurants. Restaurant owners have found that the decline in smoking caused by a tax on cigarettes has decreased their sales of meals. How would this be shown on demand and supply diagrams for cigarettes and for meals? cigarettes meals

options.A: a movement along the demand curve a shift inwards of the demand curve
options.B: a movement along the supply curve a movement along the demand curve
options.C: a shift outwards of the demand curve a shift outwards of the supply curve
options.D: a shift outwards of the supply curve a movement along the supply curve

questions.questionText: S and D show the original supply and demand curves for cola. Point X is the initial equilibrium.
Producer surplus is the difference between

options.A: the consumer surplus from the good and the producers’ total cost in supplying the good.
options.B: the highest price that the consumer would be willing to pay for the good and the price the producer actually sold it for.
options.C: the lowest price that the producer would accept for the good and the price the producer actually sold it for.
options.D: the quantity that the producers manufacture in a week and the amount sold to consumers in that week.

questions.questionText: What is an example of an externality?

options.A: Production of good X directly affects the cost of producing good Y.
options.B: The entry of a new firm reduces the profits of existing firms producing good X.
options.C: The introduction of bus-only lanes reduces the travel times of bus passengers.
options.D: The opening of a new underground railway reduces the revenue of bus operators.

questions.questionText: The table gives the estimated costs and benefits of a proposed new leisure complex. $000s private benefits 120 external benefits 80 private costs 140 external costs 20 What is the estimated value of the social benefits of the project?
The production of what is most likely to require a government cost-benefit analysis?

options.A: houses
options.B: medicines
options.C: roads
options.D: schools

questions.questionText: A national museum charges an entry fee for admission. Which combination of rival and excludable qualities would apply to visits to the national museum on a day when there are very few visitors? rival excludable

options.A: no no
options.B: no yes
options.C: yes no
options.D: yes yes

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the effects of placing a unit tax equal to AB on a good. S S A price Z G E C F B D O X Y quantity Which area represents the burden of tax paid by the producer?

options.A: ECBF B EGBF C ZABF D ZAGE

questions.questionText: Below are production possibilities for two countries showing their daily production of food and drink, each using the same quantity of resources. food drink (units) (units) country X 50 100 country Y 40 60 What can be concluded from the figures?

options.A: Country X has absolute advantage in food and comparative advantage in drink.
options.B: Country X has comparative advantage in both goods.
options.C: Country Y has absolute advantage in drink and comparative advantage in food.
options.D: Country Y has neither absolute nor comparative advantage.

questions.questionText: How might trade protection reduce a country’s ability to compete in export markets?

options.A: by increasing firms’ profit margins on goods supplied to the domestic market
options.B: by increasing the cost to the country’s manufacturers of imported components
options.C: by increasing the real disposable income of the country’s consumers
options.D: by making the country more attractive to inward investors

questions.questionText: What is found in an economic union but not in a customs union?

options.A: a common external tariff on trade with non-member countries
options.B: an absence of quotas on trade between member countries
options.C: an absence of tariffs on trade between member countries
options.D: free movement of labour and capital between member countries

questions.questionText: The table shows the balance in $million for four items in a country’s current account for two years. goods services income transfers Year 1 –72 84 –3 –24 Year 2 –87 96 12 –44 What can be concluded about the changes between Year 1 and Year 2?

options.A: Income has moved from a net inflow to a net outflow.
options.B: The difference between the value of exported and imported services has increased.
options.C: The value of exported goods has fallen.
options.D: Transfers into the country have increased.

questions.questionText: Company X reduces its workers from 250 to 200 and as a result its output decreases from 5000 to 4800 units per day. Company Y increases its workers from 800 to 1000 and as a result its output increases from 2000 to 2200 units per day. What happens to labour productivity of the workers in the two companies? company X company Y

options.A: falls rises
options.B: rises falls
options.C: rises rises
options.D: falls falls

questions.questionText: In 2012, a survey of household expenditure identified X and Y as the contents of a basket of goods for a price index. The value of the index in 2012 was 100. In 2013, the index was valued at 116. During 2013, the prices of X and Y increased by 10% and 20%, respectively. In percentage terms, which weights were attached to X and Y in calculating the index? good X good Y (%) (%)
In an economy with an interest rate of 4% per annum, the rate of inflation falls from 5% to 3% per annum. What will be a benefit of this fall?

options.A: Menu costs will fall to zero.
options.B: People on fixed incomes will be better off in real terms.
options.C: Savers will gain in real terms.
options.D: The purchasing power of the currency will rise.

questions.questionText: When is a deficit on the current account of the balance of payments likely to worsen?

options.A: when a government adopts a deflationary macroeconomic policy
options.B: when a government devalues the currency
options.C: when prices of essential imported raw materials increase significantly
options.D: when tariffs are placed on imported products with a wide range of domestic substitutes

questions.questionText: What is the real exchange rate?

options.A: the exchange rate at which foreign currency traders can buy a country’s currency
options.B: the exchange rate between a country’s currency and the US Dollar
options.C: the exchange rate with international differences in price inflation removed
options.D: the weighted average of a country’s exchange rates with its major trading partners

questions.questionText: An appreciation of country X’s currency leads to an increase in its foreign currency earnings from tourism. What can be concluded from this about the demand by foreigners for holidays in country X?

options.A: It is income elastic.
options.B: It is price elastic.
options.C: It is income inelastic.
options.D: It is price inelastic.
